135a6f7d72166abc72a0fc691651c47eb0ed1b5e.summary: ANSSI CERT-FR report (17 July 2020) on Dridex, a banking trojan that surfaced in June 2014 as a variant of Bugat. It steals online banking access codes and uses a peer-to-peer botnet run under an affiliate model. The report links Dridex development to the Evil Corp group, which it says split in April 2019, and to the BitPaymer and DoppelPaymer ransomware. Dridex is distributed through phishing botnets, Emotet, FakeUpdates and exploit kits. The report stresses that attribution is hard and that many links are only likely.

Its campaigns used phishing archives and the WinRAR vulnerability CVE-2023-38831 to deploy AllaKore RAT, DRat, Key RAT and Ares RAT, including a Linux variant. The report links SideCopy to APT36 (Transparent Tribe) through shared infrastructure and code, and attributes the campaigns with high confidence.
